\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Concentration}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Concentration
\section{Overview}
Explicit scalar identities select and evaluate the moment exponent in hypercontractive tail bounds. A positive atom parameter supplies the scaled finite-product versions.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Concentration exponent threshold]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ConcentrationAux.concentration_parameter}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $k>0$ be an integer and $t\ge(\sqrt{2e})^k$. Then $t>0$ and $t^{2/k}/e\ge2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Optimized moment identity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ConcentrationAux.concentration_optimized_moment}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $k>0$ be an integer and $t>0$, and put $q=t^{2/k}/e$. Then $((\sqrt q)^k/t)^q=\exp(-kt^{2/k}/(2e))$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Scaling a concentration threshold]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ConcentrationAux.scaled_threshold_rpow}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For an integer $k>0$ and reals $\lambda,t>0$, $(t(\sqrt\lambda)^k)^{2/k}=\lambda t^{2/k}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Scaled concentration exponent threshold]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ConcentrationAux.scaled_concentration_parameter}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ConcentrationAux.concentration_parameter, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ConcentrationAux.scaled_threshold_rpow}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k>0$ be an integer, $\lambda>0$, and $t\ge(\sqrt{2e/\lambda})^k$. Then $t>0$ and $\lambda t^{2/k}/e\ge2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Scaled optimized moment identity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ConcentrationAux.scaled_concentration_optimized_moment}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ConcentrationAux.concentration_optimized_moment, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ConcentrationAux.scaled_threshold_rpow}
\difficulty{5}
Let $k>0$ be an integer and $\lambda,t>0$, and put $q=\lambda t^{2/k}/e$. Then $((\sqrt q\lambda^{1/q-1/2})^k/t)^q=\lambda^k\exp(-k\lambda t^{2/k}/(2e))$.
\end{lemma}
